incident-bot: :rotating_light: New incident created — prod latency/throughput regression after rollout. Root: rolling deploy 2026-03-15T10:01 -> canary 10% traffic. tagging: deploy/2026-03-15/serve-runtime-v2.
cheng: seeing p95 jump and sustained throughput drop on canary slice. p50 ~120ms -> 220ms, p95 ~340ms -> 920ms. QPS down ~28% on canary hosts. kernel_fallback_count spiked.
ashley: @cheng can you paste the metrics and any logs you have? are we seeing large queue lengths or OOMs?
tim: paging on-call, I'm awake. grabbing dashboards now.
cheng: dashboard: `svc/runtime-serving/canary-10%` — batching success rate down, continuous batching window collapsed, observed many tiny batches instead of expected 16 tokens per batch. KV eviction rate ~3x baseline. attaching quick snippet: ```
[2026-03-15T10:05:12Z] req_id=abc123 latency=912ms kernel_fallback=true batch_size=1 kv_evicted=true
[2026-03-15T10:05:13Z] req_id=abc124 latency=876ms kernel_fallback=true batch_size=1 kv_evicted=true
```
marco: looks like new kernel selection logic in v2 picks slower kernel under certain sequence-length distribution. canary saw different seq-dist due to traffic sawtooth pattern.
ashley: any errors in logs besides kernel fallback? thread-local OOMs?
cheng: no OOMs, no crashes. just elevated queueing and lower throughput. autoscaler oscillating — it scaled hosts up then down repeatedly which amplified small latency blips.
ops: autoscaler saw CPU vs GPU signals mismatch. scaler policy target_util was 0.7, but the new runtime increased kernel CPU usage causing noisy signal.
marco: confirm: canary was 12% traffic, but because autoscaler rule uses host-level metrics, the oscillation affected fraction of users unevenly -> sawtooth traffic spikes.
ashley: customer impact? any 5xxs or user-facing errors?
cheng: 5xxs minimal (~0.2% increase), but tail latency > 1s for heavy prompts. two enterprise customers on single region reported degraded response times via CS.
tim: tagging for severity: Sev-2 (customer impact, partial). initiating on-call handoff to infra SREs.
incident-bot: @tim assigned incident-5291 to oncall-tim. runbook: runtime-regression -> triage -> mitigations.
marco: immediate mitigations we can try: 1) flip feature flag for new kernel selector (ff:runtime_v2_kernel_selector=false), 2) abort rollout (rollout abort deploy/2026-03-15/serve-runtime-v2), 3) stabilize autoscaler (set target_util to 0.55) 4) temporarily increase min replicas for canary slice.
ashley: I'd prefer kill the kernel selector FF first (fastest) — it's a config flip without rolling binaries. if that fails, abort rollout.
cheng: attempting FF flip now via console toggle. ```
# pseudocommand shown for audit
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' \ 
  https://console.api.internal/flags/runtime_v2_kernel_selector -d '{"value":false}'
```

marco: also preemptively pin canary to smaller instance type? maybe not until we see FF effect.
